To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tight junction protein Occludin is a potential target for tight junction modulation, and that the first extracellular domain of Occludin can be used for tight junction modulation by the use of a lipopeptide principle.

peptides from the extr cellular loops of occludin can be used as a principle to modulate tight junction permeability and that the lipoamidation of the peptides increases the effect and makes them more stable.

peptides corresponding to the first extracellular loops of occludin, which are located on the extracellular side of the tight junction, increased the permeability in the tight junctions of Caco-2 monolayers, and that the lipopeptide derivative C14-OP 90-103, in which OP 90-103 is attached to the C14-lipoamino acid at the N terminus, displayed a rapid increase in tight junctions permeability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of tight junction modulating peptides.
the discovery and development of novel peptide-based tight junction modulators for use as drug carriers.

the development of a new principle for modulating tight junction permeability, which could be used to increase the bioavailability of drugs that are otherwise limited by their poor permeability through the tight junctions of the intestinal epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the l-isomer of C14-occludin peptide 90-103 is a promising candidate as a tight junction modulator.
the lipoamidation of the N terminus with a lipoamidic acid (C14-) of 14 carbon atoms is a new principle for the modulation of tight junctions based on occludon peptides.
the peptide C14-OP 90-103 represents an interesting prototype of a new tight junction modulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tight junctions can be opened and closed using peptides from the extrellular loops of occludin.
the extracellular domains are accessible and that the tight junctions can be modulated by peptides from the extracelluar loops of occludin.
the tight junction protein, occludin, has an important role in regulating the paracellular barrier function of the epithelia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the extracellular domain of occludin is accessible to peptides and can be used for tight junction modulation, which opens up new avenues for tight junction modulation and for the development of new drugs for the treatment of intestinal diseases such as Crohn's disease.

tight junction modulation can be achieved by peptides derived from extracellular loops of tight junction proteins, and that the lipopeptide derivative C14-OP-90-103 is an example of a new class for tight junction modulators.

the lipoamido acid derivative of the peptide OP90-103, C14- OP90-103 is an efficient modulator of the tight junction permeabilty in Caco- 2 cells and may be a promising lead compound for the development of tight junction modulatory agents.
